what_was_read: a2-path's edit at 0.268, 0.579 and 0.786 of its size: each of its 18 matrices set to the original plus that fraction of a2-path's stored change, rounded to BF16. Each model answered the 60 questions of the overlap and round one's 28 on its own, greedy, on GPU0, and was judged as every rung is. The three models were not kept: each is exactly the original, a2-path's model and the fraction. No fit, no traces.

curves.meaning: Per fraction and group. 0 is the original model (wrong: none complete, all 30 subtract the descent; correct: all complete) and 1 is a2-path itself.

prediction_vs_result.leaving_the_opening: Not as computed. 27, 49 and 51 of the 60 answers of the overlap write another token than the original within their first 20 steps at 0.268, 0.579 and 0.786, not a quarter, a half and three quarters (54 at the whole edit). The crossing computed at one token underestimates it: at 0.268, 12 answers leave at step 11, a second close choice.
prediction_vs_result.correct_answers: Not as predicted, and in the other direction. 15, 22 and 21 of the 30 correct answers break at the three fractions, against 12 at the whole edit. Correct answers that keep their original opening do not all stay complete either: 10 of 16 at 0.268, 5 of 7 at 0.579, 5 of 6 at 0.786.
prediction_vs_result.wrong_answers: The reading that was left open. The subtraction of the descent falls with the size of the edit: 30, 13, 2, 2, 1 of the 30 still subtract it at 0, 0.268, 0.579, 0.786 and 1. Complete answers do not follow the size: 0, 7, 5, 8, then 17 at the whole edit.
prediction_vs_result.would_weaken_it: Both construction readings occurred. Correct answers break at least as often at 0.268 as at the whole edit, and they break while keeping their original opening, so the damage is not a matter of size in the way this run supposed. And no fraction repairs more than it breaks (7 complete against 15 broken, 5 against 22, 8 against 21; the whole edit: 17 against 12), so a smaller step of this edit is not a way to stabilize it. By the declaration, what separates repair from damage is then the direction of the change, which is C2's and D2's question. Neither weighs on the hypothesis.

failures_only.note: Every answer at every fraction: its fields before and after, the first step at which it writes another token than the original, and its length.

what_this_changes: A fraction of a2-path is not a gentler a2-path. Complete answers of the overlap, wrong then correct, at 0, 0.268, 0.579, 0.786 and 1 of its size: 0 and 30, 7 and 15, 5 and 8, 8 and 9, 17 and 18. The whole edit is far better than 0.786 of it in both groups.

The calculation the edit aims at responds to its size in a graded way (30, 13, 2, 2, 1 answers still subtract the descent). Whole-answer completeness does not, and which answers break or are repaired changes from one size to the next: 6 correct answers break at every size and 3 at none; 1 wrong answer is complete at every size and 7 at none. The count of complete answers of one edited model is one draw of something that moves a great deal between neighbouring models; a difference between two rungs in that count needs to be read with that in mind.
Leaving the original text early does not decide the damage: at 0.268, 6 of the 12 correct answers that kept their opening and left their text later broke (Astra's reading of the same file).

A likely reason a fraction does worse, not tested here: a2-path's matrices were fitted in path order, each on what the ones before it left at full size, so at a fraction every later matrix meets inputs it was not fitted for. If so, a rate of change for this construction has to sit inside the build, each matrix fitted on what the scaled earlier ones leave, and cannot be applied to a finished edit. That is a question for the next round (Marcos, November 10: find the right rate, optimizer and solver in the redo).
